# @mission-platform/rxjs

Framework-neutral RxJS integration for Mission Platform. It is authored **once**
against the `@mission-platform/jsx` neutral hooks and compiled to both React and
Vue by `@mission-platform/vite-plugin-jsx`, so a single write-once component can
compose event/data streams with the full RxJS operator vocabulary and render
their values on either framework. Observables flow into component state, and
subscriptions are tied to the component's effect lifecycle so nothing leaks on
unmount.

Its only runtime dependencies are `rxjs` and `@mission-platform/jsx`; `react`,
`react-dom`, and `vue` are optional peers supplied by the consuming app.

## Exports (`@mission-platform/rxjs`)

### Observable → component state (`src/use-observable.ts`)
- `useObservable(source)` / `useObservable(source, initialValue)` — subscribe to
  an `Observable` and return its latest emission as component state (via the
  neutral `useState` + `useEffect`). Returns `undefined` (or the seed) until the
  first emission; unsubscribes on unmount.

### Subscription lifetime (`src/use-subscription.ts`)
- `useSubscription(subscribe, dependencies?)` — run a `subscribe` factory after
  mount (via the neutral `useEffect`) and unsubscribe from its `Unsubscribable`
  result on unmount / dependency change.
- `useSubscribe(source, observerOrNext?, dependencies?)` — subscribe to an
  `Observable` for the component's lifetime in one step.
- `Unsubscribable` — the `{ unsubscribe(): void }` shape accepted above.

## Authoring model
Because the hooks compile per-framework, the **neutral baseline** used at
authoring time (and in SSR / the runtime adapters) is render-once: `useState`
returns its initial value and `useEffect` is a no-op, so a component using these
composables renders the initial/seed value identically on React and Vue. The
live subscription behaviour comes from the per-framework hooks the build-time
plugin swaps in.

## Consumers
Any write-once Mission Platform component (see `@mission-platform/components`)
that needs debounced inputs, `switchMap`-style request cancellation,
`combineLatest` derivations, or other stream orchestration while rendering the
result on both frameworks.
